content.title: Determining if a Relation is a Function
content.overview: A relation is a set of ordered pairs that links inputs to outputs. On the ACT, you must distinguish between general relations and functions. A function is a specific type of relation where every input (domain element) is paired with exactly one output.
learning_objectives: Define the difference between a relation and a function.
Identify the domain elements (inputs) and range elements (outputs) in a set of ordered pairs.
Apply the Domain-Output Pair Scan to determine if a relation qualifies as a function.
Recognize common traps involving repeated outputs versus repeated inputs.

sections.title: The Definition of a Function
sections.content: A relation is simply any set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a stricter type of relation. For a relation to be a function, every input value must map to exactly one output value. If you see the same input value paired with two or more different output values, the relation fails the definition and is not a function.

sections.title: The Domain-Output Pair Scan
sections.content:
To determine if a relation is a function, follow these steps: 1. List every distinct input (x-value) present in the relation. 2. For each input, identify all the outputs (y-values) it is paired with. 3. Check for violations: If any single input is paired with more than one unique output, the relation is NOT a function. 4. Verify: Ensure every pair in the original set was checked.

![A flow chart showing the steps to determine if a relation is a function: Identify Inputs, Map to Outputs, Check for Multiple Outputs per Input, and Determine Function Status.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/bb5c49c4-d4fd-4537-b3de-9610064eede2-1786505821105-244.webp)

sections.title: Repeated Outputs vs. Repeated Inputs
sections.content: A common point of confusion is the 'direction' of uniqueness. A function allows multiple different inputs to result in the same output (e.g., both 2 and -2 squaring to 4). However, a function NEVER allows one input to result in multiple different outputs. If the x-value repeats with different y-values, it is not a function. If the y-value repeats with different x-values, it can still be a function.

worked_examples.question: Determine if the following relation is a function: {(1, 5), (2, 10), (3, 15), (2, 20)}
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the inputs (x-values). The inputs are 1, 2, 3, and 2. Step 2: Map inputs to outputs. Input 1 maps to {5}. Input 2 maps to {10, 20}. Input 3 maps to {15}. Step 3: Check for violations. Input 2 is paired with two different outputs (10 and 20). Step 4: Conclusion. Because input 2 has more than one output, this relation is NOT a function.

worked_examples.question: Is the relation {(4, 7), (5, 7), (6, 8)} a function?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the inputs. The inputs are 4, 5, and 6. Step 2: Map inputs to outputs. Input 4 maps to {7}. Input 5 maps to {7}. Input 6 maps to {8}. Step 3: Check for violations. Each input (4, 5, and 6) is paired with exactly one output. Step 4: Conclusion. Even though the output 7 is repeated for different inputs, each input has only one output. Therefore, this IS a function.

common_mistakes: Thinking a relation is not a function just because an output (y-value) repeats.
Failing to notice a repeated input if the ordered pairs are not listed in numerical order.
Assuming all sets of ordered pairs are functions by default.
exam_tips: Scan the x-coordinates first. If all x-coordinates are unique, it is automatically a function.
If you see a mapping diagram, look for any input that has two or more arrows pointing away from it; that indicates it is not a function.
On a table, look for duplicate values in the 'x' column. If they exist, check if their 'y' values are different.
content.recap: A function is a relation where every input has exactly one output. To test this, scan for repeated inputs; if an input repeats with a different output, the relation is not a function. Repeated outputs are perfectly acceptable in a function.

knowledge_claims.content: A relation is defined as any set of ordered pairs consisting of inputs and outputs.
A function is a specific type of relation where each input corresponds to exactly one output.
A relation fails to be a function if a single input is paired with two or more different outputs.
The first step in the Domain-Output Pair Scan is to list every distinct input (domain element) from the relation.
In a function, multiple different inputs can share the same output, but one input cannot have multiple different outputs.
If every x-coordinate in a set of ordered pairs is unique, the relation is guaranteed to be a function.
It is a mistake to conclude a relation is not a function simply because the same y-value appears more than once.
In a mapping diagram, a relation is not a function if any single input value has multiple arrows originating from it.
To verify a relation is a function, you must confirm that no domain element appears with two different outputs.
The relation {(1, 2), (1, 3)} is not a function because the input 1 is associated with two different outputs, 2 and 3.
The relation {(2, 5), (3, 5)} is a function because each distinct input (2 and 3) has exactly one output (5).
In a table of values, a function is identified by ensuring that every time an x-value repeats, the corresponding y-value is identical.
